rules.ind7: Indian-language reads: Wikipedia views in the 12 Indian editions (hi ta te kn ml mr bn gu pa or as bh), 7 UTC days. English is never in this total. '≥' = a floor from the daily most-read lists (top 1,000 per edition; a day off the list counts 0) — no 60-day curve yet.
rules.en_in: English reads FROM India: India's per-country most-read list (all editions), English rows, 7 days. Wikimedia rounds these up, so each listed day is a ceiling. A day off the list is unknown (0 up to that day's list cutoff), so a title listed on only some days shows a range: listed days … + the cutoff of each day off the list. '≤' only when it is on the list all 7 days.
rules.en_world: English Wikipedia worldwide, 7 days — read around the world, so it is KEPT OUT of the Indian total.
rules.change: Indian-language reads vs the 7 days before. Curves only: '—' for a floor.
rules.stage: From the 30-day curve: At peak (last day = 30-day high) · Building (last 3 days ≥ 70% of peak and +15% on the 3 before) · Cooling (below 70% of peak and −15%) · Elevated (holding at 3× its 30-day median) · Steady · Faded. Floor only = no curve. No stage word = a death reported in the last 30 days.
rules.zone: Where the Indian-language reading sits: South = Tamil + Telugu + Kannada + Malayalam editions; Hindi; ≥ 60% = that zone, both ≥ 30% = Both, else '-leaning'. Only with enough reads to split.
rules.agreement: Signals rising: reading (last day ≥ 1.5 × the median of the 7 before; needs a curve) and Google Trending now (on a scan in the last 7 days). 'quiet' = none.
rules.confidence: High = clears an edition floor with articles in ≥ 2 Indian editions, or ≥ 300 Indian reads a day · Med = clears a floor or ≥ 100 a day · Low = otherwise. Floors: Hindi 300 a day; any other edition 20% of that edition's leader this week (≥ 50 in 7 days).
rules.editions: Indian editions with an article on this entity (of 12).
rules.consistent: The newest dated event on file — calendar, Wikidata release / death, Google trending, a main-page feature or the 60-day high. 'Consistent with', never 'because'.
rules.kept: Kept: film, series, web series, song, entertainment person, athlete, sports event or team (Wikidata P31 / P106, or the tracker's registry), with an India link. Politics, places, generic pages and deaths of anyone else are dropped. Held back: writers, poets and spiritual figures (a secondary screen or music occupation is not enough), sport topic pages with no dated event (Cricket, FIFA, Olympic Games) and adult-search traps in any script.
rules.days: Wikimedia days are UTC and publish about a day late.

chart_rules.reads: Most-read on Wikipedia, 7 UTC days — not viewers. Indian-language editions (hi ta te kn ml mr bn) + English: English FROM India (India's per-country most-read list, a ceiling) for a non-Indian title; English WORLDWIDE for an Indian title (read mostly in India, but the India share is unknown). The basis is on every row. '≥' = a floor from the daily most-read lists (no 60-day curve yet). A title on India's list only some days shows a range (a day off the list is unknown, up to that day's cutoff): ranked on its low end only while the top is within 25% of it, otherwise listed, not ranked.
chart_rules.rank: Rank within the tab by 7-day reads (most-read on Wikipedia, never 'most watched'), among titles streaming on the platform now: a rights-only or upcoming title is listed, never ranked. Movement = vs the rank the 7 days before would give (curves only).
chart_rules.change: All editions with a 60-day curve: these 7 days vs the 7 before. '—' without a curve. For a title read on English from India the worldwide English curve is kept out (no India curve exists: '—').
chart_rules.latest: Latest = new on the platform in the last 90 days (OTT date, newest season start, premiere), plus TV serials running now ('Airing': on air, not new) and films with no OTT date released in theatres in the last 120 days (streaming or rights sold).
chart_rules.new: New = arrived on the platform in the last 7 days: the newest of its OTT date there, its newest season start and its premiere (a running serial's airing never counts).
chart_rules.stage: From the 30-day curve: At peak (last day = 30-day high) · Building (last 3 days ≥ 70% of peak and +15% on the 3 before) · Cooling (below 70% of peak and −15%) · Elevated (holding at 3× its 30-day median) · Steady · Faded. Floor only = no curve. No stage word = a death reported in the last 30 days.
chart_rules.source: Where the platform link comes from: List (the platform's Wikipedia list page) · Category (its originals category) · TV channel (a channel's show streams on the broadcaster's app; running or aired in the last 2 years) · Film list (a film from Wikipedia's 'List of <language> films of <year>' whose article names the platform in a streaming sentence) · Article (a film the reading board / calendar found, same sentence rule) · Rights map (the tracker's own calendar / rights facts — they win over Wikipedia).
chart_rules.reach: How Airtel reaches the platform (verified partner pages): ₹99 Xstream Play card · ₹279 (Netflix, JioHotstar, ZEE5 bundle; or an app only on the ₹279 card) · ₹149 Xstream Play Premium Pack (terms only) · Prime plans (prepaid ₹838 / ₹1,199) · free app · not via Airtel.
chart_rules.official: Netflix's official India Top 10 for its latest week (Mon–Sun): the title's rank there. Shown to check the Wikipedia method — never used to rank.
chart_rules.match: How many of Wikipedia's own top 10 (Films / TV, Netflix titles, the same Mon–Sun week) are on Netflix's official India Top 10. 'In catalogue' = official titles the Wikipedia catalogue holds at all.
chart_rules.share: Each platform's part of the 7-day reads of the ranked titles on this page, all tabs (a title on two platforms gives each half). Only titles Wikipedia links to a platform count: apps with thin Wikipedia lists (many ₹99-card apps) and sport (not tracked here) are under-covered.
chart_rules.arrivals: Films whose article (or the rights map) gives an OTT date in the next 30 days.
chart_rules.no_deal: Films in theatres (released in the last 120 days) read this week whose article names no streaming home (and the rights map has none). Reads on this page's rule (the same one the table ranks on — see the rule line): Indian editions + English from India or worldwide; each figure's tip names its basis. A film with no reads this week is not listed.
